{{short description|Convex polygon with pairs of equal, parallel sides}}
[[File:Octagon g2 symmetry.png|thumb|upright|Octagonal zonogon]]
[[File:Centrosymmetric hexagonal tiling.svg|thumb|[[Tessellation]] by irregular hexagonal zonogons]]
[[File:Dissected octagon.svg|thumb|upright|[[Regular octagon]] tiled by squares and rhombi]]

In [[geometry]], a '''zonogon''' is a [[central symmetry|centrally-symmetric]], [[convex polygon]].{{r|bms}} Equivalently, it is a convex polygon whose sides can be grouped into [[Parallel (geometry)|parallel]] pairs with equal lengths and opposite orientations, the two-dimensional analogue of a [[zonohedron]], or the two-dimensional case of a [[zonotope]].

==Examples==
A [[regular polygon]] is a zonogon if and only if it has an even number of sides.{{r|ys}} Thus, the square, regular hexagon, and regular octagon are all zonogons.
The four-sided zonogons are the square, the [[rectangle]]s, the [[rhombus|rhombi]], and the [[parallelogram]]s.

==Tiling and equidissection==
The four-sided and six-sided zonogons are [[parallelogon]]s, able to tile the plane by translated copies of themselves, and all convex parallelogons have this form.{{r|aa}}

Every <math>2n</math>-sided zonogon can be tiled by <math>\tbinom{n}{2}</math> [[parallelogram]]s.{{r|beck}} (For equilateral zonogons, a <math>2n</math>-sided one can be tiled by <math>\tbinom{n}{2}</math> [[rhombus|rhombi]].) In this tiling, there is a parallelogram for each pair of slopes of sides in the <math>2n</math>-sided zonogon. At least three of the zonogon's vertices must be vertices of only one of the parallelograms in any such tiling.{{r|mo}} For instance, the regular octagon can be tiled by two squares and four 45° rhombi.{{r|gnf}}

In a generalization of [[Monsky's theorem]], {{harvs|first=Paul|last=Monsky|authorlink=Paul Monsky|year=1990|txt}} proved that no zonogon has an [[equidissection]] into an odd number of equal-area triangles.{{r|monsky|ss}}

==Other properties==
In an <math>n</math>-sided zonogon, at most <math>2n-3</math> pairs of vertices can be at unit distance from each other. There exist <math>n</math>-sided zonogons with
<math>2n-O(\sqrt{n})</math> unit-distance pairs.{{r|af}}

==Related shapes==
Zonogons are the two-dimensional analogues of three-dimensional [[zonohedra]] and higher-dimensional zonotopes. As such, each zonogon can be generated as the [[Minkowski sum]] of a collection of line segments in the plane.{{r|bms}} If no two of the generating line segments are parallel, there will be one pair of parallel edges for each line segment. Every face of a zonohedron is a zonogon, and every zonogon is the face of at least one zonohedron, the prism over that zonogon. Additionally, every planar cross-section through the center of a centrally-symmetric polyhedron (such as a zonohedron) is a zonogon.
